sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Pacific Engagement Visa (PEV) - Treaty stream (Tuvalu) pre-application ballot gives eligible people from Tuvalu equal access to the PEV Treaty stream (Tuvalu). The ballot provides a fair and transparent process by randomly selecting people to apply for the visa. It makes sure there is equal access for people of any:

- skill level
- occupation
- gender.

The Australian Government will allocate up to 280 Treaty stream places to Tuvalu nationals each year. This includes partners and dependent children.

To be able to apply for the Pacific Engagement visa (subclass 192) - Treaty stream (Tuvalu), you must first register in the Treaty stream ballot. If we randomly select you in the Treaty stream ballot, you can then apply for the visa. To find out if you can register in the ballot, see Ballot eligibility.

There is a ballot registration fee of AUD25.

sections.heading: The Pacific Engagement visa (subclass 192) - Treaty stream process
sections.text:
- Ballot opens
Tuvalu nationals will have a separate ballot for the Treaty stream (Tuvalu). The department will publish details of the ballot on the Treaty stream (Tuvalu) Country Ballot Status page.

- Register in the ballot
When a ballot is open, eligible citizens can submit a registration through ImmiAccount. You cannot register before or after this period.
- Ballot selection (selected)
After the ballot registration period closes, the department will run a selection process for Tuvalu. We will share ballot selection periods (open and close dates) for when the random selection of registrations will happen on the Treaty stream (Tuvalu) Country Ballot Status page. The department will send randomly selected participants a Notification of Selection letter.
- Apply for the visa
Selected participants can use the link provided in the Notification of Selection letter to apply. Participants must apply on or before the invitation expiry date provided in the letter.
